description:
The Swami Vivekananda Merit-cum-Means Scholarship is a significant initiative by the Government of West Bengal. 

It was launched in 2016. 

The scheme is named after Swami Vivekananda, a prominent figure in Indian philosophy and spirituality. 

The primary objective of the scholarship is to provide financial assistance to students from economically weaker sections. 

It aims to promote higher education among meritorious students. 

The scholarship targets students pursuing undergraduate and postgraduate courses. 

The scheme is designed to ensure that financial constraints do not hinder the educational aspirations of deserving students. 

The scholarship covers various fields of study including engineering, medicine, arts, and commerce. 

The total amount of scholarship awarded can vary based on the level of education. 

For undergraduate courses, the scholarship amount is ₹10,000 per year. 

For postgraduate courses, the scholarship amount is ₹20,000 per year. 

The scholarship is renewable each year based on the student’s performance. 

Students must maintain a minimum attendance of 75% to be eligible for renewal. 

The eligibility criteria for the scholarship are specific and detailed. 

Applicants must be residents of West Bengal. 

They should have completed their higher secondary education from a recognized board. 

For undergraduate courses, students must have secured at least 75% marks in their higher secondary examination. 

For postgraduate courses, a minimum of 53% marks in the undergraduate degree is required. 

The family income of the applicant must not exceed ₹2.5 lakh per annum. 

This income limit is crucial for determining eligibility. 

The application process for the Swami Vivekananda Merit-cum-Means Scholarship is straightforward. 

Students can apply online through the official website of the West Bengal Government. 

The application form must be filled out with accurate personal and academic details. 

Applicants are required to upload necessary documents. 

These documents include income certificates, mark sheets, and proof of residence. 

The application period typically begins in July each year. 

The deadline for submitting applications is usually in August. 

After the application submission, the verification process begins. 

The verification is conducted by the concerned authorities in the respective educational institutions. 

Once verified, the scholarship amount is disbursed directly to the bank accounts of the beneficiaries. 

The disbursement usually occurs in September or October. 

The implementing authority for this scholarship scheme is the Department of Higher Education, Government of West Bengal. 

They oversee the entire process from application to disbursement. 

Students can contact the department for any queries regarding the scholarship. 

The contact details for the Department of Higher Education are available on their official website. 

The scheme has seen a significant uptake since its inception. 

In the academic year 2020-2021, over 1 lakh students benefited from the scholarship. 

The total amount disbursed during that year was approximately ₹200 crore. 

This reflects the government's commitment to enhancing educational opportunities for all. 

The scholarship not only provides financial support but also encourages students to excel academically. 

It fosters a competitive spirit among students from diverse backgrounds. 

The scheme has been instrumental in reducing dropout rates in higher education. 

Many students have reported improved academic performance due to the financial assistance provided. 

The scholarship also aims to empower students by promoting self-reliance. 

By alleviating financial burdens, students can focus more on their studies. 

The initiative aligns with the broader goals of the Indian government to promote education. 

It complements various other schemes aimed at improving literacy and educational outcomes. 

The Swami Vivekananda Merit-cum-Means Scholarship is a vital tool for social equity. 

It ensures that quality education is accessible to all, regardless of economic status. 

The scheme has been positively received by students and educational institutions alike. 

Feedback from beneficiaries indicates high levels of satisfaction with the support provided. 

The scholarship has also encouraged many students to pursue higher studies in fields previously considered inaccessible. 

In conclusion, the Swami Vivekananda Merit-cum-Means Scholarship plays a crucial role in shaping the educational landscape of West Bengal. 

It not only provides financial support but also inspires a generation of students to strive for excellence. 

The initiative reflects the commitment of the West Bengal government towards inclusive education. 

By supporting meritorious students from economically weaker sections, the scheme contributes to the overall development of society. 

It is a testament to the belief that education is a powerful tool for change. 

The scholarship continues to evolve and adapt to the needs of students. 

Future enhancements may include increased scholarship amounts or expanded eligibility criteria. 

The government remains focused on ensuring that no deserving student is left behind. 

Overall, the Swami Vivekananda Merit-cum-Means Scholarship is a commendable effort towards fostering educational growth in West Bengal.
